\section[l'attaccante]{l'attaccante — forward, striker}

\label{lesson:IT-C510-attaccante}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for penalty, then the Italian for to book.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'attaccante}
\textbf{l'attaccante} — \textquotedblleft{}forward, striker\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il nostro attaccante è il più veloce del campionato.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Our striker is the fastest in the league.}
\end{quote}

From \emph{attaccare} \textquotedblleft{}to attack\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{attaccante} is built on \emph{attaccare} \textquotedblleft{}to attack, to attach\textquotedblright{}; the origin of \emph{attaccare} is not settled, though a Germanic word for a stake is often suggested.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'attaccante}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'attaccante}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'attaccante}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for penalty, then the Italian for to book, then say \emph{l'attaccante} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does l'attaccante mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Forward, striker\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[il difensore]{il difensore — defender}

\label{lesson:IT-C510-difensore}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to book, then the Italian for forward.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il difensore}
\textbf{il difensore} — \textquotedblleft{}defender\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il difensore ha fermato l'attaccante.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The defender stopped the striker.}
\end{quote}

In court it is also the lawyer for the defence.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{difensore} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{dēfēnsor} \textquotedblleft{}a defender\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{dēfendere} \textquotedblleft{}to ward off\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il difensore}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il difensore}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il difensore}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to book, then the Italian for forward, then say \emph{il difensore} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does il difensore mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Defender\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[il centrocampista]{il centrocampista — midfielder}

\label{lesson:IT-C510-centrocampista}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for forward, then the Italian for defender.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il centrocampista}
\textbf{il centrocampista} — \textquotedblleft{}midfielder\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Gioco come centrocampista nella squadra della scuola.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I play midfield in the school team.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{centrocampo} \textquotedblleft{}midfield\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{centrocampista} is built on \emph{centro} \textquotedblleft{}centre\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{centrum}, and \emph{campo} \textquotedblleft{}field\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{campus} (Lewis \& Short), with \emph{-ista}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for forward, then the Italian for defender, then say \emph{il centrocampista} again

\section[il titolare]{il titolare — first-team player; holder, owner}

\label{lesson:IT-C510-titolare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for defender, then the Italian for midfielder.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il titolare}
\textbf{il titolare} — \textquotedblleft{}first-team player; holder, owner\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Oggi gioco titolare, non in panchina.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Today I am in the starting line-up, not on the bench.}
\end{quote}

Also the owner of a shop: \emph{il titolare del bar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{titolare} is a learned borrowing from Late Latin \emph{titulāris} \textquotedblleft{}of a title\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{titulus} \textquotedblleft{}an inscription, a title\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for defender, then the Italian for midfielder, then say \emph{il titolare} again

\section[parare]{parare — to save (a shot); to ward off}

\label{lesson:IT-C510-parare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for midfielder, then the Italian for first-team player.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: parare}
\textbf{parare} — \textquotedblleft{}to save (a shot); to ward off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il portiere ha parato un tiro difficile.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The goalkeeper saved a difficult shot.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La parata} — a save. Also \emph{parare un colpo} — to ward off a blow.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{parare} is inherited from Latin \emph{parāre} \textquotedblleft{}to prepare, to make ready\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); the sense \textquotedblleft{}to ward off\textquotedblright{} grew from getting ready to meet a blow.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{parare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for midfielder, then the Italian for first-team player, then say \emph{parare} again
\end{itemize}

To sweat? (\textbf{sudare}.) Referee? (\textbf{l'arbitro}.) To whistle? (\textbf{fischiare}.) Foul? (\textbf{il fallo}.) Penalty? (\textbf{il rigore}.) To book? (\textbf{ammonire}.) Forward?
